Remark
[Euclidean isometries as a matrix group]

Source: petersen:page-0052 ↗ def:pet-ch1-isometry-group ↗ ex:pet-ch1-isometry-group-euclidean

1. ch1:1.6.9Identify $\mathbb {R}^n$ with the hyperplane $x^{n+1}=R$ in $\mathbb {R}^{n+1}$. Then $\operatorname {Iso}(\mathbb {R}^n)$ is represented by \[ \left[\begin{smallmatrix} O & v \\ 0 & 1 \end{smallmatrix}\right], \qquad O\in O(n),\quad v\in \mathbb {R}^n, \] and these are precisely the linear maps preserving that hyperplane and the degenerate form $x^1y^1+\cdots +x^ny^n$.
